case.context: mazeed sells accounting, tax and e-invoicing software to small and mid-size businesses in the UAE and Saudi Arabia.
case.challenge: It had to look as trustworthy as a bank and move as fast as a startup.
case.direction: I inherited the wordmark and the core colours. My job was everything around them: how the purple, the mint and the chevron behave across hundreds of assets in English and Arabic. That meant a creative direction for 2026 built on a competitive read of QuickBooks, Xero and Zoho Books, one layout for three products, a 16-icon service system, and bilingual ads that are mirrored for right-to-left reading rather than translated. Single campaign systems reached 80 assets across two languages and five formats.

title: AYWA
kind: Brand identity for a fintech app
line: Identity for a card and money app for Egypt's 16 to 28 year olds. Aywa is the loud Egyptian yes.
meta: Wordmark, symbol, card design, app, campaign, out-of-home, social

case.year: TODO: year or years of the project
case.context: TODO: optional. Who the client is and the situation before you started.
case.challenge: TODO: the brief in one or two sentences. What problem did the client (or you) need solved?
case.direction: The idea is money in colour. Your money splits into five pockets, and the colours from the photography become those pockets: pink for going out, volt for main, orange for food, blue for saving and chrome for bills. Each pocket gets its own virtual card, so you always see where your money goes.
case.system: AYWA opens an account in four minutes with no branch, then lets you tap to pay, send in seconds and split a bill in one tap. The identity runs on one rule, the Lean: everything tilts 10° forward. The custom wordmark has no vertical strokes, and the centre of the W breaks the cap line by 18%. That peak becomes the app symbol and the hero of the card.

meta: Arabic wordmark, colour system, packaging, campaign posters, social, motion

video.caption: Brand in motion: the identity system animated.

case.year: TODO: year or years of the project
case.context: TODO: optional. Who the client is and the situation before you started.

case.direction: In Arabic, jahd (جهد) means both electrical voltage and human effort. VULT sits exactly between the two, and the whole identity is built on that coincidence.
case.system: The old Latin wordmark with its gradient was replaced by an Arabic wordmark: four letters carried on a single wire, with a spark drawn into the lam. Six flat colours, no gradients, and a set of single-word Arabic headlines carry it from can to poster to the feed. The case study itself is written in Arabic, on purpose.

title: roava
line: A specialty coffee brand that is calm and loud at once: soft lavender, broken by one lime accent.
meta: Logo, colour, pattern, packaging, signage, campaign, social

case.year: TODO: year or years of the project
case.context: TODO: optional. Who the client is and the situation before you started.
case.challenge: A coffee brand that feels calm and loud at once.
case.direction: The answer was a system of restraint. Three soft purples do the quiet work, ink carries the type, and lime appears once per composition, never twice.
case.system: The rounded wordmark hides a coffee bean inside the o, with three strokes of steam above it. An arcade pattern borrowed from the shopfront is built from one module and always rises from the bottom edge, across cups, pouches, bags, signage and the feed.
